recovery: A dedicated Docker daemon and dedicated containerd use a tmpfs data root to avoid the host disk writeback stall.
network: Host networking for container runs and tool image builds; default networking for cached root-image builds. The dedicated daemon manages no bridge or iptables.
root_image: Built from the unchanged repository Dockerfile and original cached layers with USER_ID=1002, GROUP_ID=1002 and default build networking. Original image manifest sha256:1682337d156eec2607c9533df38e97722f4d40651dc1be2fafaab90ef2f8ff35; config sha256:6bb0db03610e5bb97fa6db4717eef917366e234b4a61a0a930be07b684a2ea9d.
safe4u_base: Imported the exact pre-existing safe4u:latest OCI image (sha256:d4258e0e12ad6ffb62e0e95321af5922cb00fefc1ef5420ed1c7e0261c1868d7) directly from the local containerd content cache using docker image load; source cache was read-only.
toolchain_caches: Existing patched Rust/KLEE/MIRScan build directories are preserved and mounted from the repository.
system_docker: Docker/containerd were restarted during recovery. Previously exited containers auto-started by restart policies were stopped again; baseline running-container list was empty.
temporary_cache_cleanup: Only unused failed-build cache in the dedicated tmpfs daemon was pruned to reclaim 6.843 GB. Original Docker images, original BuildKit caches and repository toolchain caches were preserved.
cleanup: Both dedicated daemons were stopped; their private network-namespace handle was unmounted and their verified private tmpfs directory removed. Results, source snapshots, image identities, library hashes and original host caches are retained.
